newsitem.title: USA: Dun & Bradstreet targets 1997 net growth 5-7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Dun & Bradstreet targets 1997 net growth 5-7 pct.

text.p: Dun & Bradstreet Corp on Wednesday reiterated its goal of increasing earnings by five to seven percent in 1997.
But the company noted in a news release that its first two quarters represented less than a third of that goal and it still is working on what it described as key issues.
Among them are the performance of its yellow pages directory business, the Dun & Bradstreet operating companies outside the United States and the company's "Year 2000" expenses.

Dun & Bradstreet reported second quarter earnings per share of $0.29, including an $0.02 per share charge for the write-off of its minority investment in Nets Inc. The year-ago figure was $0.27 per share. The First Call consensus Wall Street analysts' estimates was $0.29.
The company said its growth was driven by a strong performance at Moody's Investors Service, which had revenues up 21 percent to $110.2 million.
But revenue for the Directory Information Services segment was down one percent to $64.1 million, the company said.
